headline_marked: [[Anthropic defies Pentagon ultimatum]] on AI use for surveillance and autonomous weapons
headline: Anthropic defies Pentagon ultimatum on AI use for surveillance and autonomous weapons
summary: Anthropic's CEO refused to remove usage restrictions on its Claude AI for mass surveillance and autonomous weapons. The US government retaliated by banning all federal agencies from using Anthropic's products and designating it a "supply chain risk."
details: On February 26, 2026, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published a statement refusing the US Defence Secretary's ultimatum to remove usage restrictions from its Claude AI model. This decision fractured the relationship between Silicon Valley and the Pentagon. The ultimatum demanded unrestricted use by February 27, 2026.

The restrictions were specific: Claude AI must not be used for mass domestic surveillance of American citizens, nor for powering fully autonomous weapons systems capable of selecting and engaging targets without human oversight. Amodei stated that frontier AI systems are not reliable enough for such applications.

Retaliation was swift. On February 27, President Donald Trump directed all federal agencies to cease using Anthropic's products. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth designated the company a "supply chain risk," an unprecedented classification for an American firm.

Hours later, rival OpenAI announced a deal with the Pentagon to provide its AI technology for classified networks. This confrontation has become a defining test case for who determines the ethical boundaries of AI in warfare.

The dispute originated in July 2025 when the Department of War awarded Anthropic a $200 million contract, making Claude the first frontier AI system cleared for classified military networks. OpenAI, Google, and xAI also received contracts.

This partnership contained a structural tension from the start, as Anthropic's acceptable use policy prohibited mass domestic surveillance and fully autonomous weapons, terms the Department of War initially agreed to. Six months later, these terms were deemed unacceptable.

The catalyst was Hegseth's January 2026 AI strategy memorandum, which declared the military would become an "AI-first warfighting force." It mandated that all AI procurement contracts incorporate "any lawful use" language, reframing vendor-imposed safety guardrails as obstacles to national security.

The memo's philosophical orientation was captured by the line: "The risks of not moving fast enough outweigh the risks of imperfect alignment." This consciously inverted the precautionary principle that had previously governed American military AI policy.

Hegseth demanded "unfettered" access to Claude without guardrails, rejecting Anthropic's compromises, including allowing use for missile defense programs. Anthropic's refusal places it in a complex position, defending civil liberties while facing government sanctions.

headline_marked: [[GTA 6 preorders begin tonight]] at midnight local time; Standard & Ultimate editions available
headline: GTA 6 preorders begin tonight at midnight local time; Standard & Ultimate editions available
summary: Digital preorders for Grand Theft Auto VI start tonight, offering Standard ($79.99) and Ultimate ($99.99) editions, both including a month of GTA+ subscription.
details: Grand Theft Auto VI preorders are set to go live tonight at midnight local time in the US. Fans can secure either the Standard Edition for $79.99 or the Ultimate Edition for $99.99. Both digital variants include a one-month GTA+ subscription as a bonus.

The Standard Edition features the base game, a Vintage Vice City Pack with retro cosmetics, and the '55 Vapid Stanier vehicle. The Ultimate Edition expands on this with extra side missions, additional vehicles, weapons, and a wide array of outfits and cosmetics for characters Jason and Lucia.

The highly anticipated sequel to Grand Theft Auto V is officially slated for a November 19 release. Its launch is expected to be a major event, with reports of workplaces planning shutdowns and other publishers rescheduling their releases to avoid competition.
PC gamers, however, will face a wait of approximately one year before the game becomes natively available on their systems. This delay means console players will get first access to the title.
